__comment: Editable places content. Add objects to items with id, name, category, area, description, openingHours, entryFee, priceType, and mapsUrl.

items.name: Tower of London
items.description: A thousand years of royal history, Crown Jewels, ravens, battlements, and brilliant Yeoman Warder tours beside the Thames.
items.openingHours: Usually daily 9:00-17:30; hours vary by season
items.entryFee: Paid ticket, book ahead for best slots

items.name: Buckingham Palace
items.description: The King's official London residence, best paired with St James's Park and the ceremonial Changing of the Guard.
items.openingHours: Exterior daily; State Rooms open selected summer dates

items.name: Big Ben
items.description: London's most recognisable clock tower, officially the Elizabeth Tower, with classic views from Westminster Bridge.

items.name: London Eye
items.description: A slow 30-minute riverfront rotation with sweeping views across Westminster, St Paul's, and the city skyline.

items.name: Tower Bridge
items.description: Victorian engineering at its grandest, with blue suspension towers, glass walkways, and bridge lift moments.

items.name: St Paul's Cathedral
items.description: Christopher Wren's masterpiece, with a vast dome, crypt, whispering gallery, and one of London's best skyline climbs.

items.name: Trafalgar Square
items.description: A civic stage framed by fountains, Nelson's Column, galleries, statues, and fast walks to Soho and Westminster.

items.name: Houses of Parliament
items.description: Neo-Gothic riverside drama and the heart of UK politics, beautiful from both Westminster and Lambeth bridges.
items.openingHours: Exterior all day; tours on selected dates

items.name: National Gallery
items.description: World-class paintings by Van Gogh, Turner, Monet, and Da Vinci in a landmark gallery overlooking Trafalgar Square.

items.name: British Museum
items.description: A vast collection of global history, from Egyptian sculpture to the Rosetta Stone, set around a spectacular Great Court.

items.name: Victoria and Albert Museum
items.description: Design, fashion, sculpture, ceramics, jewellery, and architecture inside one of London's most elegant museums.

items.name: Natural History Museum
items.description: Dinosaur galleries, glittering minerals, grand architecture, and family-friendly science displays in a cathedral-like hall.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; book timed entry

items.name: Tate Modern
items.description: Modern art in a converted power station, with monumental installations and a river walk to Shakespeare's Globe.

items.name: Royal Observatory Greenwich
items.description: Stand on the Prime Meridian, explore timekeeping history, and enjoy wide views over Canary Wharf and the Thames.

items.name: Kew Gardens
items.description: UNESCO-listed botanical gardens with glasshouses, treetop walks, seasonal blooms, and a calm west London escape.
items.openingHours: Daily; closing time varies by season

items.name: Hampton Court Palace
items.description: Henry VIII's Tudor palace with grand kitchens, formal gardens, maze, riverside walks, and a full day-trip feel.

items.name: Windsor Castle
items.description: A royal day trip from London with State Apartments, St George's Chapel, and a handsome riverside town nearby.

items.name: Hyde Park
items.description: London's famous central park for boating, cycling, picnics, Speakers' Corner, and a graceful walk to Kensington Gardens.

items.name: Regent's Park
items.description: Formal gardens, open lawns, sports pitches, and nearby Primrose Hill make this one of London's loveliest green days.

items.name: Covent Garden
items.description: Street performers, boutiques, theatres, restaurants, and polished piazza energy in the heart of the West End.
items.openingHours: Area open all day; shops and restaurants vary

items.name: Leadenhall Market
items.description: A covered Victorian market with ornate paintwork, elegant shopfronts, pubs, and strong Harry Potter photo appeal.
items.openingHours: Public access daily; shops mainly weekday daytime

items.name: Kyoto Garden
items.description: A serene Japanese-style garden with koi ponds, waterfalls, maples, and a quiet mood minutes from Notting Hill.

items.name: Postman's Park
items.description: A peaceful pocket garden known for the moving Watts Memorial to Heroic Self-Sacrifice.

items.name: God's Own Junkyard
items.description: A glowing warehouse of neon signs and pop-art colour, excellent for photos and paired with nearby breweries.

items.name: Crossbones Garden
items.description: A small memorial garden with ribbons, gates, and local history honouring London's outcast dead.
items.openingHours: Open at limited times; check before visiting

items.name: Little Venice
items.description: Canals, narrowboats, waterside cafes, and a gentle towpath walk towards Camden or Paddington Basin.

items.name: Leake Street Graffiti Tunnel
items.description: A legal street-art tunnel under Waterloo Station, constantly changing and lively after South Bank walks.

items.name: Columbia Road Flower Market
items.description: A colourful Sunday street market full of flowers, independent shops, cafes, and East End character.

items.name: Bermondsey Street
items.description: Independent restaurants, galleries, design shops, and an easy route to White Cube, Maltby Street, and Tower Bridge.
items.openingHours: Street open all day; businesses vary

items.name: Neal's Yard
items.description: A tiny colourful courtyard tucked between Covent Garden and Seven Dials, loved for cafes and wellness shops.

items.name: Dennis Severs' House
items.description: An immersive time-capsule house where rooms feel paused mid-story, atmospheric and unlike a standard museum.

items.name: Leighton House Museum
items.description: A richly decorated artist's home with an extraordinary Arab Hall, tiles, paintings, and quiet garden rooms.

items.name: Pergola and Hill Garden
items.description: A romantic elevated pergola wrapped in greenery, perfect with a Hampstead Heath walk.
items.openingHours: Daily from morning; closing varies seasonally

items.name: Millennium Bridge at Sunset
items.description: Frame St Paul's across the river as the light drops, then continue to Tate Modern or the South Bank.

items.name: Borough Market Archway
items.description: Historic railway arches, market signs, and food stalls create a lively London backdrop.

items.name: Primrose Hill Skyline View
items.description: A classic panoramic view of central London, especially good at sunrise or golden hour.

items.name: St Dunstan in the East
items.description: Bombed-out church ruins transformed into a leafy public garden, atmospheric between skyscrapers.

items.name: Southbank at Night
items.description: Reflections, bridges, theatre lights, riverside performers, and glowing views toward Westminster.
items.openingHours: Open all day; best after dusk

items.name: Sky Garden
items.description: A free indoor garden high above the City, with skyline terraces and views to the Shard and Tower Bridge.

items.name: Alexandra Palace
items.description: Sweeping hilltop views, a grand Victorian palace, parkland, food stalls, and events.
items.openingHours: Park open daily; venue hours vary

items.name: Greenwich Park Hill View
items.description: A graceful hilltop view across maritime Greenwich, the Thames, Canary Wharf, and the City beyond.

items.name: Science Museum
items.description: Interactive galleries on space, medicine, engineering, and technology, ideal for families and rainy days.
items.entryFee: Free general admission; book timed entry

items.name: Thames Path Walk
items.description: Walk river sections from Westminster to Tower Bridge for landmarks, bridges, public art, and skyline views.

items.name: Changing of the Guard
items.description: A ceremonial favourite with music, marching guards, and big crowds; arrive early for a clear view.
items.openingHours: Usually late morning on selected days; check schedule
